turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in, Mrs Lang. The computer's playing up, so give me a second. Right. What brings you in today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you for seeing me, doctor. I have been unusually tired, and I feel the cold much more than I used to.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long have the tiredness and the cold been going on?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): A good four months. I have been inclined to blame the workload, and my age. I am fifty-three, and the stamina is not what it was.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): What work are you doing these days?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I manage the accounts team at a logistics firm. I am there past six most evenings, so I had put the tiredness down to the hours.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is that tiredness there all day?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Most of the day, I'm afraid. I get home and I could sleep in the chair before dinner. My husband says I am not myself.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, can you say that again? I had the wrong tab open.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Of course. I am tired for most of the day, and I could sleep in the chair before dinner. My husband feels I am not myself.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): How has your mood been, then?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Rather low. I don't look forward to things, and I am a little tearful in the evenings. I have put that down to work as well.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any thoughts of harming yourself?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none at all. I would tell you immediately if that were the case.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Has your weight gone up or down?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): It has gone up, close to four kilograms since the winter. I have not been eating more. I often skip lunch at my desk.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about the bowels?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): I have been constipated for a couple of months. I go every second or third day, which is not my usual at all.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the motion, or pain when you go?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No blood, and no pain.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain, or are you short of breath on the stairs?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): The office is dreadfully cold, even this month. I sit under the air-conditioning vent, and I have taken to wearing a cardigan indoors. It seems excessive for November.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): I meant chest pain and breathlessness. Do you get either of those?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain, and I am not short of breath. I apologise, I had answered the wrong question.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any palpitations, or the heart racing?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I have not noticed anything of that sort.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any change in your hair or your skin?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): My skin is a little dry on the shins. My hair is quite unchanged.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is there thyroid disease in the family?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): My mother had an underactive thyroid and took thyroxine for many years. She died in 2016, from a stroke.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you ever had a thyroid blood test yourself?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, at my previous surgery they said it was borderline, though I was never given a number. I cannot date it properly, three years ago or perhaps four.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): People do misremember the word borderline, and the old result will not load, so I will not treat that as a firm figure. We should simply repeat the test.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I may have the wording wrong, though I am sure a test was done. I would not wish to mislead you, doctor.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): The nurse has entered rosuvastatin, 10 milligrams at night. Is that the dose you take?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm sorry, I believe that is not correct. I take 20 milligrams by mouth at night, for my cholesterol. The nurse may have kept the earlier dose.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Say the dose once more? I lost the end of it.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Twenty milligrams, by mouth, every night. It was increased from 10 last year, and I am certain the dose is 20.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll leave the dose blank until I see the packet. Your cholesterol is on the history and still ongoing, yes?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, it has been there for some years. I take the tablet every night, and I do not miss doses.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines, or to anything else?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): None that I am aware of.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or drink?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): I have never smoked. I have one glass of wine with Sunday lunch, and nothing beyond that.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): This bloods form is still spinning. Was the traffic heavy on the way? The freeway was a proper car park.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): It was most trying, I'm afraid. I allowed extra time and still waited twenty minutes near the exit. I do hope I have not put your list behind.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not at all. Half the morning list was late anyway. Did you catch any of the cricket last night?
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Only a little of the Test, while my husband had it on. The bowling looked very accomplished, though I do not follow the field placements.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): They're forecasting storms for Saturday, which is a nuisance. My brother's got tickets for the day.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): We have my grandson staying for the weekend. He is seven, and terribly set on feeding the ducks at the park, so a storm would disappoint him.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let's hope the ducks get their visit. The screen is back. The nurse recorded your blood pressure at 136 over 82, pulse 70, and weight 89.5 kilos.

[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your neck feels soft, with no goitre. Your hands are cool, and the pulse is regular. This may be an underactive thyroid, or it may simply be the long hours and getting older. I can't separate those today, so I am not making a diagnosis.

[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll arrange a blood test for thyroid function and for cholesterol. Come back in two weeks and we'll go through the results. If you feel markedly worse, come in sooner. Please bring the rosuvastatin box from the chemist so we can sort the 10 from the 20.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I shall bring the box, and I will speak to reception about the return visit on my way out.

spec.situation: Middle-aged person tired and cold for months, weight up, constipated, low mood; pins it on work and age; mother had thyroid disease; one old thyroid test result recalled wrongly ('borderline, they said'). Blood test planned.
features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Prior thyroid test was done; 'borderline' was patient-reported and explicitly uncertain.
bad.text: Thyroid blood test reported as borderline (type=laboratory, status=completed)

bad.reason: Planned thyroid function test is stated; indication wording is inferred, not explicitly given.
bad.text: Thyroid function blood test (type=laboratory, status=planned, requested_by=doctor, indication=To distinguish underactive thyroid from long hours and age)

omissions.text: Rosuvastatin dose is recorded incompletely/wrongly: patient specifically said she takes 20 mg by mouth every night, increased from 10 mg last year, and is certain of the 20 mg dose.
Tiredness is present most of the day, not just before dinner.
Low mood includes anhedonia: she does not look forward to things.

Previous thyroid blood test history is recorded too definitively: patient said she was told it was 'borderline' at a previous surgery about 3-4 years ago, but doctor stated this should not be treated as a firm figure because old result would not load and people may misremember the word.
Neck examination finding that the neck felt soft was stated by the doctor.
